questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ohun ti a n pe ni afoniwasi ninu ede Yoruba?
options: Ohun ti a n pe pelu didena emi lenu (consonants)
Oro ti n fi han igbese
Ohun ti a n pe lai dena emi lenu (vowels)
Ami ti a n fi han ibeere
questions.explanation: Vowels (afoniwasi) in Yoruba are speech sounds produced without significant obstruction of airflow, unlike consonants (kọnsonanti), which involve some closure or narrowing in the vocal tract.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ohun ti a n pe pelu didena emi lenu ninu ede Yoruba?
questions.explanation: Consonants (kọnsonanti) are produced by partially or fully obstructing airflow at some point in the vocal tract, in contrast to the more open articulation of vowels.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Afoniwasi melo ni o wa ninu ede Yoruba boṣewa?
questions.explanation: Standard Yoruba is generally described as having seven oral vowel sounds (a, e, ẹ, i, o, ọ, u), along with additional nasalised vowels.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ami ti a n lo lati fi han bi a se n pe oro ga tabi ki lo silẹ ninu ede Yoruba?
questions.explanation: Tone marks (ami ohun) indicate the pitch pattern of syllables in written Yoruba, an essential feature since tone can change a word's entire meaning.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ohun elo melo ni Yoruba n lo lati fi han ohun ninu ede naa?
options: Meta: ohun oke, ohun aarin, ati ohun isale (high, mid, and low tone)
questions.explanation: Yoruba phonology is fundamentally built around three tone levels: high, mid, and low, forming the basic tonal system used to distinguish word meanings.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ilana ti afoniwasi kan ba parẹ nigba ti oro meji ba ti sopọ ninu gbolohun (elision)?
questions.explanation: Vowel elision (isunki vaweli) is a phonological process where a vowel sound is dropped when two words come together in speech, common in fluent Yoruba pronunciation.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe mimu oro kan kuro patapata ninu gbolohun nitori idi asayan (deletion)?
questions.explanation: Deletion refers to the complete omission of a sound or word element under certain phonological conditions, distinct from elision, which specifically involves vowel reduction.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe apa ti gbolohun ede ti o ni afoniwasi kan ti a n pe ni akoko kan naa?
questions.explanation: A syllable (alusilo) is a unit of pronunciation typically organised around a single vowel sound, which may be preceded by one or more consonants.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini abajade ti o wọpọ nigba ti a ba fi ohun oke si oro ti o gbọdọ ni ohun isale, ninu apeere bi 'oko' (farm) ati 'oko' (husband, pẹlu ohun ti o yatọ)?
options: Oro naa a di afoniwasi nikan
Oro naa a maa dawọ lati je oro
Iyipada ninu itumọ oro naa patapata
questions.explanation: Since Yoruba is a tonal language, changing the tone pattern on an otherwise identical sequence of letters can completely change the word's meaning, as in the contrast between 'oko' (farm) and 'ọkọ' (husband/vehicle).

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini isẹ akọkọ ti a n ṣe ninu iwadi Fonọlọji ninu ede Yoruba?
options: Iwadi ohun ede ati bi a se n to wọn sọtọ ninu oro ati gbolohun
questions.explanation: Phonology (Fonọlọji) is the branch of language study focused on the sound system of a language and how those sounds are systematically organised within words and sentences.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini idi pataki ti a fi n kọ awọn ọmọ ile-iwe nipa ami ohun ninu ede Yoruba?
options: Nitori ko si idi kankan to ye
Ki won le ma lo ami ohun rara
Nitori ami ohun ko ni ipa kankan lori itumọ
Ki won le ka ati ko ede naa ni ọna to peye, nitori pe ami ohun le yi itumọ oro pada
questions.explanation: Teaching tone marks is essential because Yoruba is a tonal language, where the correct tone can be the difference between two entirely different words or meanings.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe eto ninu eyi ti a n to awọn ohun kọ jọpọ lati mọ bi won ṣe n sise ninu ọrọ sisọ?
questions.explanation: Phonology (Fonọlọji) is specifically the study of how sounds pattern and function together within a language, as opposed to grammar, literature, or culture.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ọrọ isọ meji ti a ba so pọ lati fi han ohun kan pataki, bi 'gb' ninu 'igba'?
questions.explanation: A consonant digraph is a combination of two letters representing a single distinct sound, such as 'gb' in Yoruba, common in the Yoruba alphabet.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini idi to ye ki a mo daju iyato laarin afoniwasi imu (nasalized vowels) ati afoniwasi lasan ninu ede Yoruba?
options: Nitori afoniwasi imu ko si ninu ede Yoruba
Nitori afoniwasi imu maa n yato ni itumọ ati bi a se n ka won
Nitori won je oro kan naa nigbagbogbo
questions.explanation: Nasalised vowels in Yoruba are distinct sounds produced with airflow through the nose, and distinguishing them correctly from oral vowels is important for accurate pronunciation and meaning.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe oro ti n so oruko eniyan, ibi, tabi nkan kan ninu ede Yoruba?
questions.explanation: A noun (oro-oruko) is a word class used to name a person, place, thing, or idea, a fundamental word category in Yoruba grammar.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe oro ti n so ise tabi iṣẹlẹ kan ninu ede Yoruba, bi 'lọ' tabi 'jẹ'?
questions.explanation: A verb (oro-ise) expresses an action or occurrence, such as 'lọ' (go) or 'jẹ' (eat), forming the core predicate of a Yoruba sentence.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe oro ti n ṣàpèjúwe oro-oruko kan ninu ede Yoruba, bi 'dara' tabi 'buburu'?
questions.explanation: An adjective (oro-aponle) describes or modifies a noun by attributing a quality to it, such as 'dara' (good) or 'buburu' (bad).

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ilana ti a n gba lati da oro tuntun ninu ede Yoruba (word formation)?
questions.explanation: Word formation (Iṣẹda ọrọ) is the morphological process of creating words in Yoruba, including through compounding, reduplication, and other structural methods.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe oro ti a mu wa lati ede miran wọle sinu ede Yoruba, bi oro ti a mu lati ede Gẹẹsi?
questions.explanation: Loan words (ọrọ àyálò) are terms borrowed from another language, such as English, and incorporated into Yoruba vocabulary.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe oro ti n ṣàpèjúwe oro-ise, oro-aponle, tabi oro-atokun miran ninu ede Yoruba (adverb)?
questions.explanation: An adverb modifies a verb, adjective, or another adverb, typically indicating manner, time, or degree in a Yoruba sentence.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe oro ti n dipo oro-oruko ninu gbolohun, bi 'o' tabi 'won'?
questions.explanation: A pronoun (oro-nfiropo) stands in place of a noun, such as 'o' (he/she/it) or 'won' (they), avoiding repetition of the noun itself.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe oro ti n so ipo ohun kan si ohun miran ninu gbolohun, bi 'lori' tabi 'labẹ'?
questions.explanation: A preposition (oro-atokun) indicates the relationship, often of place or time, between a noun and another element in the sentence, such as 'lori' (on) or 'labẹ' (under).

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe gbolohun ti o pe ni kikun to ni eni ti n se ise (subject) ati ise ti won n se (predicate)?
questions.explanation: A complete sentence (gbolohun) consists of a subject (the doer or topic) and a predicate (what is said about the subject), forming a grammatically complete statement.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ọrọ ti n so 'ati' tabi 'sugbon' ti n so gbolohun meji pọ ninu ede Yoruba?
questions.explanation: A conjunction (oro-asopọ) links words, phrases, or clauses, such as 'ati' (and) or 'sugbon' (but), showing the relationship between the connected elements.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini isẹ akọkọ ti a n ṣe ninu iwadi Girama ninu ede Yoruba?
options: Iwadi bi a ṣe n to awọn oro jọ lati mọ gbolohun to pe
questions.explanation: Grammar (Girama) is the area of language study concerned with how words are correctly combined and arranged to form grammatically sound sentences.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini gbolohun aṣẹ (imperative sentence) ninu ede Yoruba, bi 'Lọ si ile-iwe!'?
options: Gbolohun ti n fun ni aṣẹ tabi ibeere
questions.explanation: An imperative sentence issues a command or request, such as 'Lọ si ile-iwe!' (Go to school!), distinct from a statement or question.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe gbolohun meji tabi ju bẹẹ lọ ti a ba so pọ pẹlu oro-asopọ ninu ede Yoruba?
questions.explanation: A compound sentence joins two or more independent clauses using a conjunction, combining related ideas of equal grammatical weight.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe mimu oro meji sopọ mọ ara won lati da oro tuntun kan silẹ (compounding), bi 'ile' ati 'iwe' di 'ile-iwe'?
questions.explanation: Compounding is a word formation process where two or more independent words are joined together to create a new word with its own meaning, such as 'ile' (house) and 'iwe' (book) combining to form 'ile-iwe' (school).

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe kikọ ti n ṣàlàyé ero eniyan lori koko-ọrọ kan pẹlu ẹri ti n gbe ero yẹn ga (argumentative essay)?
questions.explanation: An argumentative essay presents a clear position or opinion on a topic, supporting it with logical reasoning and evidence.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe kikọ ti n ṣàpèjúwe ibi kan tabi eniyan kan ni kikun ninu ede Yoruba (descriptive essay)?
questions.explanation: A descriptive essay vividly describes a person, place, object, or situation, using detailed language to create a clear mental image for the reader.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe kikọ ti n ro itan iṣẹlẹ kan ni ọna to tẹle ilana akoko (narrative essay)?
questions.explanation: A narrative essay tells a story or recounts a sequence of events, typically following a clear chronological structure.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe iyipada oro tabi gbolohun lati ede kan si ede miran, gẹgẹ bi lati Gẹẹsi si Yoruba?
questions.explanation: Translation (ogbufo) involves accurately converting text or speech from one language to another, requiring careful attention to both meaning and grammatical correctness.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Nigba ti a ba n ṣe ogbufo lati Gẹẹsi si Yoruba, kini o ṣe pataki julọ lati ṣe amojuto?
options: Ki a yọ ami ohun kuro patapata
Ki itumọ oro ki o dara ati pe ki gbolohun to yo jade ni oye pẹlu girama Yoruba to pe
Ki a fi ede Gẹẹsi kun inu gbolohun Yoruba
Ki a ka gbolohun kọọkan gangan bi Gẹẹsi laisi iyipada eyikeyi
questions.explanation: Good translation prioritises preserving accurate meaning while producing a sentence that follows correct and natural Yoruba grammar, rather than a rigid word-for-word rendering.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe be ti a n bere si aroko kan ninu ede Yoruba ti o n fi koko-ọrọ han kedere?
questions.explanation: The introduction (ifihan) of an essay is the opening section that clearly presents the topic and sets up what the essay will discuss.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe apakan ikẹhin ti aroko kan ninu ede Yoruba ti n ṣàkópọ ohun ti a ti sọ?
questions.explanation: The conclusion (ipari) summarises the essay's main points and provides a closing statement, wrapping up the discussion presented in the body.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini idi pataki ti a fi n ko ẹkọ Aroko ati Ogbufo ninu idanwo Yoruba?
options: Lati mọ agbara won lati ṣe iṣiro
Lati mọ agbara ọmọ ile-iwe lati ṣe alaye ero won ni kikọ ati lati yi ede pada ni ọna to pe
Lati mọ agbara won lati sise oko
Lati mọ agbara won lati kọrin nikan
questions.explanation: Essay writing and translation skills assess a student's ability to express ideas clearly in writing and accurately convert meaning between languages.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Nigba idanwo Fahimta, kini a n reti lọwọ akẹkọ lẹhin ti o ba ka ẹsẹ kan?
options: Ki o dahun ibeere lori ohun ti o ti ka ati loye rẹ
Ki o ko ẹsẹ tuntun kan dipo
Ki o yi ẹsẹ naa pada si ede miran patapata
questions.explanation: Comprehension exercises require the reader to understand the meaning and details of a passage and accurately answer related questions about it.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe koko-ọrọ pataki tabi ero akọkọ ti onkọwe kan n gbiyanju lati fi han ninu ẹsẹ kan?
questions.explanation: The main idea or theme represents the central message that the author is primarily trying to convey through the passage.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ninu idanwo Fahimta ti JAMB fun Yoruba, iru ẹsẹ meji wo ni a maa n lo?
questions.explanation: The JAMB Yoruba comprehension section typically includes both a prose passage and a verse (poetic) passage, testing the student's ability to interpret central themes from both forms.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini o yẹ ki akẹkọ ṣe ti ko ba loye itumọ oro kan gangan bi a ti lo o ninu ẹsẹ kan?
options: Ko wo bi oro naa ṣe baamu pelu iyoku gbolohun lati mọ itumọ rẹ nibẹ
Ko lo itumọ oro naa lati inu iwe itumọ Gẹẹsi laisi ero si ọrọ inu ẹsẹ naa
questions.explanation: Understanding a word's meaning within context requires examining how it fits with the surrounding sentence, since many words carry different meanings depending on usage.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe agbara lati ṣàkópọ ẹsẹ gigun kan sinu alaye kukuru ti o ni ohun pataki ninu rẹ?
questions.explanation: Summarising involves condensing a longer passage into a brief statement that captures its most essential points, without including every minor detail.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ninu ẹsẹ ẹwi (verse passage), kini o yẹ ki akẹkọ ṣe akiyesi rẹ ju bi ninu ẹsẹ arọ lasan?
options: Ọjọ ti a ti kọ ẹsẹ naa nikan
Lilo ede ati aworan (imagery) ti a lo lati fi han ero jinlẹ
Iye oro ti o wa ninu ẹsẹ naa nikan
questions.explanation: Poetic passages often use figurative language and vivid imagery to convey deeper meaning, requiring careful attention beyond a literal reading, unlike straightforward prose.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini o ṣe pataki lati ṣe ki a to dahun ibeere ninu idanwo Fahimta?
options: Ka ẹsẹ naa daradara ki a to bere si dahun ibeere
Dahun ibeere ki a to ka ẹsẹ naa
questions.explanation: An effective comprehension strategy involves thoroughly reading the passage first before attempting to answer any questions, ensuring accurate understanding of the content.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ibeere ti n beere lati mọ ohun ti a ko sọ ni gbangba ninu ẹsẹ ṣugbọn ti a le mọ lati inu awọn ami inu rẹ (inference)?
questions.explanation: Inference questions require the reader to deduce information that is implied rather than explicitly stated, using contextual clues within the passage.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe Litereso Alenu ninu asa Yoruba?
options: Litereso ti a mu wa lati ede miran
Litereso ti a kọ sinu iwe nikan
Litereso ti a n gbe kalẹ ni ẹnu, ti a ko kọ sile
questions.explanation: Oral literature (Litereso Alenu) refers to literary traditions transmitted verbally from generation to generation, rather than through written texts, including proverbs, riddles, and praise chants.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ọrọ kukuru ti o ni ọgbọn tabi otitọ ti a n lo ninu ọrọ sisọ lojoojumọ, bi 'Bi a ba n gun igi, a n wo isalẹ'?
questions.explanation: A proverb (owe) is a short, traditional saying expressing widely accepted wisdom or truth, passed down through generations within Yoruba society.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ere ibeere ati idahun ti a n lo lati wadi ogbọn eniyan, bi 'Kini n rin lai ni ẹsẹ?'?
questions.explanation: A riddle (alọ ọlọgbọn) is a traditional question-and-answer game designed to test cleverness and stimulate creative, logical thinking.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ọrọ pataki ti a n so lati pe agbara aiye ba wa fun idi kan pato, gẹgẹ bi aabo tabi iwosan?
questions.explanation: Incantations (ofo, sometimes associated with Ọsanyìn, the deity of herbal medicine) are traditional spoken formulas believed to invoke spiritual or mystical power for a specific purpose, such as protection or healing.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ẹsẹ tabi orin ti a n lo lati yin iyi eniyan, idile, tabi ilu kan ninu asa Yoruba?
questions.explanation: Oriki are traditional praise chants or poetry used to honour and celebrate an individual, family lineage, deity, or town in Yoruba oral tradition.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini idi to fa lilo owe ninu ọrọ sisọ Yoruba dipo ki a fi ọrọ han taara?
options: Nitori ko si ọna miran lati soro
Lati fi ibinu han taara si eniyan
Lati fi ọgbọn ati ibawi han ni ọna ti o ni itumọ jinlẹ ati ọwọ fun olutẹtisi
questions.explanation: Proverbs allow speakers to convey wisdom, advice, or subtle correction in a respectful, indirect, and often more persuasive manner than blunt direct speech.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini akoko ti a ma n ka Alọ Ọlọgbọn julọ ninu asa Yoruba atijọ?
options: Ni oru, lẹhin ti iṣẹ ọjọ ti pari
Ni ọsan nikan lakoko iṣẹ oko
questions.explanation: Traditionally, riddle-telling sessions in Yoruba communities commonly took place in the evening, providing entertainment and mental stimulation after the day's work was completed.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini ipa ti Litereso Alenu n ṣe ninu itọju itan ati asa Yoruba?
options: O n ran lọwọ lati gbe itan, iwa rere, ati ọgbọn atọwọdọwọ lati iran de iran
O n fun idaraya lasan lai ni itumọ
Ko ni ibatan kankan si itan tabi asa
O n dojukọ imọ-ẹrọ ode oni nikan
questions.explanation: Oral literature plays a vital role in preserving and transmitting a community's history, values, and traditional wisdom across successive generations.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini iyato akọkọ laarin owe ati alọ ninu ọna ti won n sise?
options: Alọ je gbolohun pipe nikan lai ni ibeere
Owe je gbolohun pipe ti o ni itumọ ni kikun, nigba ti alọ je ibeere ti o nilo idahun ti o ni ogbọn
Won je ohun kan naa lai si iyato
questions.explanation: Proverbs are complete, standalone statements of wisdom, while riddles are structured as an interactive question requiring a clever answer, making them distinct forms within oral literature.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini ipa ti awọn agbalagba n ṣe ninu titọju ati fifiranṣẹ Litereso Alenu ninu awujọ Yoruba?
options: Won n dojukọ ere idaraya ode oni nikan
Won n ṣagbekalẹ owe, alọ, ati oriki fun awọn ọdọ ati ọmọde
Won ko ni ipa kankan ninu ọrọ yii
questions.explanation: Elders traditionally serve as the primary custodians and transmitters of oral literature, sharing proverbs, riddles, and praise chants with younger generations.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe oriki ti a n ki fun ẹnikan ni pataki lati ṣe ayẹyẹ idile tabi itan won?
questions.explanation: Oriki-orile are specific lineage-based praise chants that celebrate the history, achievements, and identity of a particular family or ancestral line.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini idi ti Ọsanyìn ṣe ni ibatan pẹkipẹki pẹlu Ofo ninu asa Yoruba?
options: Ọsanyìn ko ni ibatan kankan pẹlu ofo
Ọsanyìn ni orisa ti a mọ si oogun ati ewe, ti won maa n pe ninu ofo iwosan
Ọsanyìn je orukọ oba kan atijọ
questions.explanation: Ọsanyìn is traditionally recognised as the deity associated with herbal medicine and healing, closely linked to incantations (ofo) invoked for medicinal and protective purposes.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ewi ti a n ka ni gbangba pẹlu ohun orin tabi ilu ti n ba a lọ ninu asa Yoruba?
questions.explanation: Ewi refers to a distinctive Yoruba tradition of performed oral poetry, often chanted or recited with musical or rhythmic accompaniment.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini iyato akọkọ laarin Litereso Alenu ati Litereso Kiko?
options: Litereso Alenu ni a n kọ sinu iwe nikan
Litereso Kiko ni a n gbe kalẹ ni ẹnu nikan
Ko si iyato kankan laarin awọn mejeeji
Litereso Alenu ni a n gbe kalẹ ni ẹnu, nigba ti Litereso Kiko ni a n kọ sinu iwe
questions.explanation: The fundamental distinction lies in the mode of transmission and preservation: oral literature is passed down verbally, while written literature is recorded in text form.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini idi pataki ti a fi n ṣe iwadi Litereso Alenu ninu eto eko JAMB fun ede Yoruba?
options: Ki awọn akẹkọ le loye ati mọriri asa ati ọgbọn ibile awọn baba won
Ki won kọ ede miran dipo
questions.explanation: Studying oral literature helps students understand and appreciate the cultural heritage and traditional wisdom of their ancestors, an important educational goal at the JAMB level.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini o wọpọ laarin owe, alọ, ati oriki gẹgẹ bi apa kan ti Litereso Alenu?
options: Won je oro ti a mu wa lati ede miran
Gbogbo won je akọọlẹ ti a kọ sinu iwe
Gbogbo won je ọna ikosile ti a n gbe kalẹ ni ẹnu ti o gbe iye asa Yoruba jade
Won ko ni ibatan kankan si asa Yoruba
questions.explanation: Proverbs, riddles, and praise chants are all forms of orally transmitted expression that collectively embody and communicate Yoruba cultural values and wisdom.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini o le fa ki eniyan ma loye itumọ jinlẹ ti owe kan ti a ba ko mọ asa ti o wa lẹhin rẹ?
options: Nitori gbogbo eniyan ni oye kanna nipa owe
Nitori owe ko ni itumọ kankan ni gbogbo igba
Aini imọ nipa asa ati ipo ti a lo owe naa
Nitori owe je oro tuntun nikan
questions.explanation: Fully grasping the deeper meaning of a proverb often requires cultural and contextual knowledge, since much of the intended wisdom relies on shared cultural understanding.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini ipa ti Ewi/Oriki n ṣe ninu ayẹyẹ gbangba ni asa Yoruba, gẹgẹ bi igbeyawo tabi isipade oba?
options: O n gbe iyi ati itan wọle sinu ayẹyẹ naa nipasẹ orin ati kikorin
Ko ni ipa kankan ninu ayẹyẹ gbangba
O n ropo iṣẹ awọn alufaa patapata
O n dojukọ iṣowo lakoko ayẹyẹ nikan
questions.explanation: Ewi and oriki performances add dignity, historical resonance, and ceremonial significance to public celebrations such as weddings or the installation of a traditional ruler.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe eniyan ti oye rẹ ninu owe, alọ, ati oriki ma n ga ninu awujọ Yoruba?
options: Akọwe (ti won ma n pe ni akewi/olowe fun ogbọn oro sisọ)
questions.explanation: Individuals skilled in the eloquent use of proverbs, riddles, and praise poetry are traditionally highly respected in Yoruba society for their verbal artistry and wisdom.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe Litereso ti a kọ sinu iwe, gẹgẹ bi arọ, ewi, ati eré ti a kọ sile?
questions.explanation: Written literature (Litereso Kiko) refers to literary works recorded in text form, such as novels, plays, and poetry collections, distinct from orally transmitted traditions.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ninu iwadi Litereso Kiko, kini a n reti lọwọ akẹkọ nipa iwe ti a yan fun u lati ka?
options: Ki o yi iwe naa pada si ede miran
Ki o ka gbogbo oro inu iwe naa lai loye rẹ
Ki o loye koko-ọrọ, awọn ohun kikọ, ati ero ti onkọwe fẹ fi han
questions.explanation: Studying a prescribed literary text requires understanding its central theme, characters, and the message the author intends to convey, rather than mere superficial reading.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe koko-ọrọ pataki tabi ero ti onkọwe kan n gbiyanju lati fi han ninu iṣẹ litereso rẹ?
questions.explanation: The theme (akori) of a literary work is its central underlying message or idea that the author seeks to convey to readers through the narrative or poetic content.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ninu Litereso Kiko, kini a n pe awọn eniyan ti n ṣe ipa ninu itan tabi eré kan?
questions.explanation: Characters (ohun kikọ) are the individuals or entities who participate in and drive the events of a literary narrative, essential to analysing prose or drama.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini ipa JAMB n ṣe ninu yiyan awọn iwe kan pato fun apa Litereso Kiko ti idanwo Yoruba?
options: JAMB n ṣe akojọ awọn iwe arọ, ewi, ati eré ti awọn akẹkọ gbọdọ ka fun idanwo naa
JAMB n ṣe akojọ orin gbajumo nikan
JAMB ko ni ipa kankan ninu eyi
JAMB n ṣe akojọ awọn owe nikan
questions.explanation: JAMB specifies a particular set of prescribed prose, poetry, and drama texts that students are expected to study in preparation for the Yoruba written literature examination.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini agbara pataki ti a nilo lati ṣe itupale (analysis) ti itan tabi eré ti a kọ sinu iwe ni ede Yoruba?
options: Agbara lati ka iwe ni yara laisi loye
Agbara lati ko iwe ẹbẹ nikan
Agbara lati ṣawari akori, ohun kikọ, ati ipo itan naa
questions.explanation: Effective literary analysis requires the ability to identify a text's theme, characters, and setting, enabling deeper understanding beyond surface-level reading.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini idi to ye ki a ma ṣe amoro alaye pataki nipa iwe kan pato ti a ko mọ daadaa ninu Litereso Kiko?
options: Nitori eyi le fa aṣiṣe ati alaye ti ko tọ nipa iwe naa
Nitori gbogbo iwe je itan kan naa
Nitori awọn akẹkọ ko nilo alaye to peye
Nitori ko si iṣoro kankan lati ṣe bẹẹ
questions.explanation: Guessing at detailed specifics of a text one is not confident about risks producing inaccurate information, which is why general, safely-known facts are preferred over unverified detail.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini o le se iranlọwọ fun akẹkọ lati loye Litereso Kiko dara ju bi o se n ka iwe lasan?
options: Fifiyesi akori, ipo itan, ati bi ohun kikọ ṣe n hu iwa jakejado itan naa
Fifiyesi nọmba oju-iwe iwe naa nikan
Fifiyesi awọ ideri iwe naa nikan
questions.explanation: A deeper understanding of written literature comes from paying close attention to theme, setting, and character development throughout the narrative, not superficial details.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe Olodumare ninu igbagbọ ibile Yoruba?
options: Ọba kan ti o ku laipe
Eleda giga julọ, orisun agbara gbogbo
questions.explanation: Olódùmarè is traditionally regarded in Yoruba belief as the Supreme Creator, the ultimate source of all power and existence.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe irunmọlẹ ninu igbagbọ ibile Yoruba?
options: Awọn orisa tabi ẹmi ti a n bọ ti n ṣiṣẹ gẹgẹ bi aṣoju laarin Olodumare ati eniyan
questions.explanation: Irúnmọlẹ̀ are traditionally understood as divine spirits or deities within Yoruba belief, often serving as intermediaries between Olódùmarè and human beings.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe emi ti a gbagbọ pe o ti ku ṣugbọn ti n farahan bi eniyan alaaye ninu igbagbọ ibile Yoruba?
questions.explanation: Akùdàáyà refers to a spirit believed in Yoruba folklore to be a deceased person who reappears in the physical world, living among the living as though still alive.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ọmọ ti a gbagbọ pe o ni ibatan pẹlu aiye ẹmi, ti o le ku laipe ti a ko ba ṣe ilana kan pato, ninu igbagbọ ibile Yoruba?
questions.explanation: Emèrè, within traditional Yoruba belief, refers to a spiritually significant child thought to have a special connection with the spirit world, sometimes associated with fragile or unusual life circumstances requiring particular rites.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini ipa Babalawo n ṣe ninu igbagbọ ibile Yoruba?
options: O n ṣiṣẹ gẹgẹ bi olori ọmọ ogun nikan
O n ṣiṣẹ gẹgẹ bi oniṣowo nikan
O n ṣiṣẹ gẹgẹ bi alufa Ifa, ti n tumọ ifiranṣẹ awọn orisa nipasẹ Ifa
O n ṣiṣẹ gẹgẹ bi agbẹ nikan
questions.explanation: A Babalawo serves as an Ifa priest, trained to interpret divine messages through the Ifa divination system, playing a central role in traditional Yoruba spiritual practice.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe eto asọtẹlẹ ibile Yoruba ti Babalawo n lo lati ba awọn orisa sọrọ?
questions.explanation: Ifa is the traditional Yoruba divination system, through which Babalawo priests interpret messages and guidance believed to come from Olódùmarè and the deities.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini Sango duro fun ninu igbagbọ ibile Yoruba?
questions.explanation: Sàngó is traditionally worshipped as the Yoruba deity associated with thunder and lightning, one of the most prominent Orisa in Yoruba religious belief.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini Ogun duro fun ninu igbagbọ ibile Yoruba?
questions.explanation: Ògún is traditionally recognised as the Yoruba deity of iron, war, and metalwork, closely associated with blacksmiths, hunters, and warriors.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini Osun duro fun ninu igbagbọ ibile Yoruba?
questions.explanation: Ọ̀ṣun is traditionally worshipped as the Yoruba goddess associated with rivers, fertility, and femininity, notably linked to the Osun River in Osun State.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini idi pataki ti igbagbọ ninu irunmọlẹ ati awọn orisa ṣe pataki to ninu asa Yoruba ibile?
options: Won n ṣe apejuwe ọna eniyan gba loye agbaye ati ipa awọn agbara giga lori aye won
Won ko ni itumọ kankan ninu igbesi aye ojoojumọ
Won je ohun kikọ itan-akọọlẹ lasan lai ni itumọ
questions.explanation: Belief in the Irunmọlẹ and Orisa traditionally shapes how Yoruba people understand the world and the influence of higher spiritual forces on their daily lives.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ilana gbigbe oye tabi ipo ọba ni asa Yoruba?
questions.explanation: Oye jíjẹ refers to the traditional institution and process of taking up a chieftaincy or kingship title within Yoruba society.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe itọju aisan ti a n ṣe pẹlu ewe ati oogun ibile ninu asa Yoruba?
questions.explanation: Ìtọ́jú aláìsàn refers to traditional Yoruba healthcare practices, often involving herbal medicine and spiritual healing methods administered by traditional healers.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe iṣẹ agbe ninu ede Yoruba?
questions.explanation: Àgbẹ̀ refers to the occupation of farming, one of the important traditional indigenous professions within Yoruba society.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe iṣẹ lilu ilu ibile ninu asa Yoruba, ti a n lo fun ijo ati ayẹyẹ?
questions.explanation: Ìlù lílù (drumming) is a significant indigenous profession and art form in Yoruba culture, essential for music, dance, and various ceremonial occasions.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe iyan ninu ede Gẹẹsi, ounjẹ ibile Yoruba ti a n gbin lati isu?
questions.explanation: Iyán (pounded yam) is a staple heritage food in Yoruba cuisine, prepared by pounding boiled yam into a smooth, dough-like consistency.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini abari ninu asa ijeun Yoruba?
options: Iru ounjẹ ibile kan ti a n pese lati agbado tabi ẹwa
questions.explanation: Àbàrí is a traditional Yoruba food dish, typically prepared from ingredients such as maize or beans, forming part of the region's heritage cuisine.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini idi to ye ki a ka oye jije si ile-iṣẹ pataki ninu asa Yoruba?
options: Nitori ko ni itumọ kankan mọ
Nitori o je ere idaraya lasan
Nitori o je iṣẹ ti awọn aṣikiri nikan n ṣe
Nitori o n pese aṣaaju ati ilana isakoso ibile fun awujọ
questions.explanation: Chieftaincy and kingship institutions traditionally provide leadership and customary governance structures essential to the organisation of Yoruba society.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini ipa awọn oniṣegun ibile n ṣe ninu itoju alaisan ni asa Yoruba?
options: Won ko ni ipa kankan ninu itoju alaisan
Won n lo iṣẹ abẹ ode oni nikan
Won n lo ewe, egbo, ati imọ ibile lati wo aisan sàn
questions.explanation: Traditional healers use herbs, roots, and inherited indigenous knowledge to treat illnesses, forming an important part of Yoruba traditional healthcare practices.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini idi ti asa isinku fi ṣe pataki ninu awujọ Yoruba?
options: O n fi ọwọ ati iyi han fun oku ẹni ti o ku, ati pe o n mu idile ati agbegbe jọ
Ko ni itumọ kankan ninu asa Yoruba
questions.explanation: Funeral customs hold significant cultural importance in Yoruba society, honouring the deceased with dignity while also bringing family and community together during mourning.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini idi ti iyan ati abari fi ka si 'ounjẹ ajogunba' (heritage foods) ninu asa Yoruba?
options: Nitori won je ounjẹ ti a mu wa lati ilu okeere
Nitori won ko ni ibatan kankan pẹlu asa Yoruba
Nitori won ti je apa pataki ninu ounjẹ Yoruba fun ọpọlọpọ iran
Nitori won je ounjẹ tuntun ti a ṣẹṣẹ da
questions.explanation: Iyán and àbàrí are considered heritage foods because they have remained central staples of Yoruba cuisine across many generations, deeply embedded in the culture's culinary tradition.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini abajade ti o le waye ti oye jije ba pẹlu ẹtọ lati sakoso ilẹ ati ọrọ awujọ ni asa Yoruba?
options: Ẹni to gba oye naa yoo di talaka lesekese
Ẹni to gba oye naa yoo ni ojuse lati darí awujọ ati pa aṣa mọ
Ẹni to gba oye naa yoo padanu gbogbo ẹtọ ilẹ rẹ
questions.explanation: Taking up a traditional title typically comes with the responsibility of providing leadership to the community and helping preserve important cultural customs and practices.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini idi to fi je ki agbe ati ilu lilu ka si iṣẹ pataki ninu asa Yoruba ibile?
options: Won je iṣẹ ti a ṣẹṣẹ ṣe agbekalẹ ni igba diẹ sẹhin
Won je ipilẹ eto-ọrọ aje ati aṣa igbesi aye awujọ ibile
Won je iṣẹ ti ko ni iye kankan
Won je iṣẹ ti awọn ọmọ ile-iwe nikan n ṣe
questions.explanation: Farming and drumming have traditionally formed the foundation of both the economic livelihood and cultural life of Yoruba communities.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe iwa rere ati iwa to peye ti a n reti lọwọ eniyan ninu asa Yoruba, ti a n pe ni 'Omoluabi'?
questions.explanation: Ìwà Ọmọlúàbí describes the concept of good character and moral uprightness highly valued in Yoruba society, encompassing qualities such as honesty, respect, and integrity.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini diẹ ninu awọn iwa pataki ti a n reti lọwọ 'Omoluabi' ninu asa Yoruba?
options: Otitọ, iteriba, ati ọwọ fun awọn agbalagba
questions.explanation: Being an Ọmọlúàbí involves embodying values such as honesty, respectfulness, and reverence for elders, central to good moral character in Yoruba culture.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Bawo ni a se ka nọmba 'ọkan' (1) ninu ede Yoruba?
questions.explanation: 'Ọkan' is the Yoruba word for the number one, the basic starting point of the Yoruba counting system.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Bawo ni a se ka nọmba 'mẹwa' (10) ninu ede Yoruba?
questions.explanation: 'Mẹwa' is the Yoruba word for the number ten, distinct from 'ogun' (twenty), 'ọgọrun' (one hundred), and 'ẹgbẹrun' (one thousand).

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Bawo ni a se ka nọmba 'ogun' (20) ninu ede Yoruba?
questions.explanation: 'Ogun' is the Yoruba word for the number twenty, a base unit in the traditional Yoruba vigesimal (base-20) counting system.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Bawo ni a se ka nọmba 'ọgọrun' (100) ninu ede Yoruba?
questions.explanation: 'Ọgọrun' is the Yoruba word for the number one hundred, distinct from 'ẹgbẹrun' (one thousand).

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Bawo ni a se ka nọmba 'ẹgbẹrun' (1,000) ninu ede Yoruba?
questions.explanation: 'Ẹgbẹrun' is the Yoruba word for the number one thousand, an important base unit for counting larger quantities.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini idi to ye ki a mọ eto kika nọmba Yoruba fun idanwo JAMB, gẹgẹ bi a ti kọ ninu eto-ẹkọ 'Òǹkà Yorùbá'?
options: Nitori nọmba Yoruba ko yato si Gẹẹsi rara
Nitori a ko lo nọmba mọ ninu ede Yoruba ode oni
Nitori idanwo naa le beere lọwọ akẹkọ lati ka tabi ka nọmba to ga bii 20,000 ni ede Yoruba
Nitori ko si idi to ye rara
questions.explanation: The JAMB Yoruba syllabus specifically covers counting numbers up to 20,000 (Òǹkà Yorùbá), reflecting the traditional Yoruba numeral system's unique structure, distinct from simple English translation.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini idi pataki ti a fi n kọ iye Iwa Omoluabi fun awọn ọmọde ninu asa Yoruba?
options: Lati je ki won gbagbe asa won
Lati kọ won ni iwa buburu
Lati kọ won ni iwa rere ti yoo ran won lọwọ lati gbe daradara ninu awujọ
questions.explanation: Teaching Ọmọlúàbí values to children aims to instil good moral character that will help them live harmoniously and respectfully within their community as they grow.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Faweli wo ninu awọn wọnyi ni a n pe ni faweli ìmú (nasal vowel), gẹgẹ bi a ṣe n lo ninu 'inú' ati 'ọ̀wọ́n'?
questions.explanation: Faweli ìmú (nasal vowels) in Yoruba, such as those represented as 'an', 'ẹn', 'un', are produced with air passing through the nose, unlike oral vowels (faweli ẹnu) which are articulated with air flowing only through the mouth.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini iyato akọkọ laarin faweli ẹnu ati faweli ìmú ninu ede Yoruba boṣewa?
options: Faweli ẹnu ni a n pe pẹlu afẹfẹ ti n gba imu la kọja, faweli ìmú si ni a n pe pẹlu afẹfẹ ti n gba ẹnu nikan
Faweli ẹnu ni a n pe pẹlu afẹfẹ ti n gba ẹnu nikan la kọja, faweli ìmú si ni a n pe pẹlu afẹfẹ ti apa kan n gba imu la kọja
Ko si iyato foonuiṣẹ kankan laarin awọn mejeeji, orukọ nikan ni o yato
Faweli ìmú nikan ni a le lo ni ibẹrẹ oro, faweli ẹnu si ni a le lo ni ipari oro nikan
questions.explanation: Oral vowels are produced with airflow passing exclusively through the mouth, while nasal vowels involve air resonating partly through the nasal cavity, a phonemic distinction that can change word meaning in Yoruba.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ninu ọrọ 'ìjà' (fight) ati 'ìjàn' (a type of fish/certain contexts nasalised), kini o fa iyato ninu itumọ awọn ọrọ meji wọnyi?
options: Iye alusilo ti o wa ninu ọrọ kọọkan
Ami ohun ti a fi si oke ọrọ kọọkan
Wiwa tabi aiwa faweli ìmú ni opin ọrọ naa
questions.explanation: The presence or absence of a nasal vowel at the end of a word can be the deciding phonemic feature that separates two otherwise similar-sounding Yoruba words with different meanings.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Iru alusilo (syllable) wo ni a rii ninu ọrọ Yoruba 'a' gẹgẹ bi ninu 'a-lá' (a dreamt)?
questions.explanation: A syllable consisting of a single vowel sound with no preceding consonant is classified structurally as a V (vowel-only) syllable, one of the basic syllable types recognised in Yoruba phonology.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Iru alusilo wo ni ọrọ 'n' fi ara han ninu 'n lọ' (I am going), ninu ẹka fonoloji Yoruba?
questions.explanation: The syllabic nasal 'n' functions on its own as a complete syllable nucleus in Yoruba, a distinct syllable type known as a syllabic nasal (N), occurring without an accompanying vowel.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ninu awọn ọrọ 'bàtà' ati 'bátà', kini o ṣe iyato itumọ awọn ọrọ meji wọnyi ti akọtọ wọn fi jọra?
options: Ilana ami ohun (tone pattern) lori alusilo kọọkan
Kikọ ọrọ pẹlu tabi lai ni olori-oro
questions.explanation: Because Yoruba is tonal, two words with identical letters can have entirely different meanings depending solely on the tone pattern marked on each syllable — a key testable distinction in Yoruba phonology.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ilana ninu eyi ti ohun kan yi pada lati je iru ohun ti o wa nitosi rẹ ninu ọrọ (assimilation), bi ninu 'iranwo' ti a le pe ni 'iranlọwọ'?
questions.explanation: Assimilation (ifisọrọ ohun) is a phonological process where a sound changes to become more similar to a neighbouring sound, distinct from elision (loss of a vowel) or deletion (loss of a whole segment).

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini iyato laarin isunki vaweli (elision) ati ifikun oro (epenthesis) ninu fonoloji Yoruba?
options: Isunki vaweli n fi ohun kun ọrọ, ifikun oro si n yọ ohun kuro
Isunki vaweli n yọ faweli kuro nigba ti oro meji ba pade, ifikun oro si n fi ohun kun ibi ti ko si tẹlẹ
Awọn mejeeji tumọ si ohun kan naa gan-an
Isunki vaweli n kan kọnsonanti nikan, ifikun oro si n kan ami ohun nikan
questions.explanation: Elision removes a vowel sound during the meeting of two words in speech, whereas epenthesis is the insertion of an extra sound into a word where none existed before — the two processes are opposites.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ninu ilana ìfohunṣọkan faweli (vowel harmony) ninu ede Yoruba, kini o n ṣẹlẹ ninu gbolohun kan?
options: Kọnsonanti n yi pada da lori faweli ti n tẹle e
Ami ohun n parẹ patapata ninu gbolohun
Faweli kan n ni ipa lori bi a ṣe n pe faweli miran ninu oro kanna, ki won le baramu ni ipo (fun apẹẹrẹ, ẹnu si ẹnu, sunmọ si sunmọ)
Alusilo n dinku ni gbogbo igba
questions.explanation: Vowel harmony in Yoruba refers to the tendency for vowels within a word to influence one another so that they share similar articulatory features, such as vowel height or advanced tongue root position.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ninu ọrọ Yoruba, ewo ninu wọnyi ṣe apejuwe pipe iṣupọ kọnsonanti meji ti a ko le ya sọtọ ni pipe (kọnsonanti didapọ)?
options: gb ninu 'igba' ati kp ninu 'akpa' (gẹgẹ bi ninu ede miran ti o jọra)
questions.explanation: Consonant digraphs like 'gb' represent single unified sounds rather than two separate consonants pronounced in sequence, a key feature distinguishing them from ordinary consonant clusters.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe iyipada ninu eyi ti ohun oke (high tone) ba yi padà di ohun sisale nitori ipa ohun ti o tele e (tone sandhi/downstep)?
questions.explanation: Downstep (ìsúnkì ohùn) is a tonal phenomenon in Yoruba where a high tone is realised at a lower pitch level due to the influence of an adjacent tone, a subtle but important feature of the tonal system.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ọrọ 'ọmọ' ati 'ọmọ̀' (ti a ba fojuinu iyato ami ohun) ṣe afihan iru iyato wo ninu fonoloji Yoruba, ti o le yi itumọ pada patapata?
options: Iyato ninu ilana ami ohun (tonemic contrast)
questions.explanation: A tonemic contrast occurs when a change purely in tone pattern, without any change in the consonants or vowels, produces a completely different word meaning — a hallmark of Yoruba's tonal phonology.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe Ọrọ-orúkọ àpapọ̀ (compound noun) tí a dá láti inú 'omo' àti 'ọba', tí ó di 'ọmọba' (prince/princess)?
questions.explanation: 'Ọmọba' is a compound noun formed by joining 'ọmọ' (child) and 'ọba' (king), a common Yoruba morphological process where two nouns combine to create a new noun with a distinct, unified meaning.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ninu ọrọ 'onímọ̀' (a person of knowledge, expert), kini ipa ti awọn ìránṣé bii 'oní-' n ṣe ninu isodipupo oro Yoruba?
options: Won n dá ọ̀rọ̀-ìse tuntun nìkan
Won n yọ oro kuro ninu gbolohun
Won n so ọrọ-orúkọ di oro-oruko titun ti n ṣàpèjúwe ẹni-nini tabi amoye ohun kan
questions.explanation: The prefix 'oní-' (or its variant 'olú-'/'ẹlẹ́') is used productively in Yoruba to derive new agentive/possessive nouns, such as 'onímọ̀' (one who possesses knowledge, an expert), from a noun base.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ìlànà ìsọdipúpọ̀ ọ̀rọ̀ nínú èyí tí a ṣe àtúnṣe apá kan ọ̀rọ̀ kan láti dá ọ̀rọ̀ tuntun sílẹ̀, bí i 'sisọ' láti inú 'sọ'?
questions.explanation: Reduplication involves repeating all or part of a word (often a verb root) to create a new word, frequently forming a gerund-like noun form in Yoruba, such as 'sisọ' (the act of speaking) from 'sọ' (to speak).

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ninu gbolohun 'Adé ra ìwé tí ó ṣeyebíye lánàá', ewo ninu awọn wọnyi ni gbolohun onigun-meta (complex sentence) fi ara han?
options: Ko si gbolohun onigun-meta ninu rẹ rara, gbolohun rọrun ni
Apa 'tí ó ṣeyebíye' je gbolohun kekere (subordinate clause) ti n ṣàpèjúwe 'ìwé'
Gbolohun naa je gbolohun idapọ (compound) nikan
Gbolohun naa ko ni oro-ise kankan
questions.explanation: A complex sentence contains at least one subordinate (dependent) clause attached to an independent clause; here, 'tí ó ṣeyebíye' is a relative clause modifying 'ìwé', making the sentence complex rather than simple.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini iyato akọkọ laarin gbolohun idapọ (compound sentence) ati gbolohun onigun-meta (complex sentence) ninu ede Yoruba?
options: Gbolohun idapọ ni gbolohun olominira meji tabi ju bẹẹ lọ ti a fi oro-asopọ dogba so pọ, gbolohun onigun-meta si ni gbolohun olominira kan pẹlu gbolohun keji ti ko le duro nikan
Gbolohun idapọ ko ni oro-asopọ rara
Gbolohun onigun-meta ni gbolohun meji olominira ti dogba pẹlu ara won nigbagbogbo
Ko si iyato kankan laarin awọn mejeeji
questions.explanation: A compound sentence links two independent (equally weighted) clauses with a coordinating conjunction, while a complex sentence pairs an independent clause with a dependent clause that cannot stand alone.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ninu gbolohun 'Bí òjò bá rọ̀, a ó dúró sí ilé', kini ipa ti apa 'Bí òjò bá rọ̀' n ṣe ninu girama gbolohun naa?
options: O je gbolohun kekere ti n ṣàfihàn ipo (conditional subordinate clause)
questions.explanation: 'Bí òjò bá rọ̀' (if it rains) functions as a conditional subordinate clause, setting a condition upon which the main clause depends, a hallmark structure in complex Yoruba sentences.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ewo ninu awọn gbolohun wọnyi ni o ṣe àpẹẹrẹ gbolohun rọrun (simple sentence) tí ó pé?
options: Adé lọ sí ọjà, ó sì ra ẹja
Adé lọ sí ọjà nítorí pé ebi ń pa á
Bí Adé bá lọ sí ọjà, yóò ra ẹja
questions.explanation: 'Adé lọ sí ọjà' (Ade went to the market) contains a single subject and predicate with no additional clause, making it a simple sentence, unlike the other options which include coordinating or subordinating structures.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe oro-ise ti o nilo oro-oruko keji (object) lati pe gbolohun naa, gẹgẹ bi 'ra' ninu 'Adé ra ìwé'?
questions.explanation: A transitive verb (oro-ise amoye) requires a direct object to complete its meaning, such as 'ra' (buy) requiring 'ìwé' (book) in 'Adé ra ìwé', unlike intransitive verbs which do not take an object.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ewo ninu awọn oro-ise wọnyi ni oro-ise alaimoye (intransitive verb), ti ko nilo oro-oruko keji lati pe itumọ rẹ?
questions.explanation: 'Sùn' (to sleep) is intransitive because it forms a complete meaning without requiring a direct object, unlike verbs like 'ra' (buy), 'rí' (see), or 'kọ' (write) which typically take an object.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ọ̀rọ̀ tí ó dúró fún ipò ọ̀rọ̀-orúkọ nínú gbólóhùn, tí ó sì ń fi hàn ẹni tí ń ní nǹkan, gẹ́gẹ́ bí 'tèmi' (mine)?
questions.explanation: 'Tèmi' (mine) is a possessive pronoun, indicating ownership in place of a full possessive noun phrase, distinct from ordinary personal pronouns or adjectives.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ninu gbolohun 'Òun fúnra rẹ̀ ni ó ṣe é', kini ipa ti 'fúnra rẹ̀' n ṣe ninu gbolohun naa?
options: O n ṣiṣẹ gẹgẹ bi oro-atokun
O n ṣiṣẹ gẹgẹ bi oro-nfiropo àrayé (reflexive/emphatic pronoun) ti n te ku sori ẹni ti n se ise
O n ṣiṣẹ gẹgẹ bi oro-ise keji
Ko ni ipa kankan ninu gbolohun naa
questions.explanation: 'Fúnra rẹ̀' functions as a reflexive/emphatic pronoun construction, emphasising that the subject performed the action personally, a nuanced grammatical feature in Yoruba pronoun usage.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe iru gbolohun ti a n lo lati fi han iyalẹnu tabi ero ti o le, gẹgẹ bi 'Hà! Kí nìdí tó fi rí báyìí!'?
questions.explanation: An exclamatory sentence expresses strong emotion such as surprise or shock, often marked by an exclamation, distinct from declarative, interrogative, or imperative sentence types.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ka ẹsẹ yi: 'Ojú ọjọ́ ti bẹ̀rẹ̀ sí í yí padà ní abúlé Ìjẹ̀bú. Àwọn àgbẹ̀ ti dáwọ́ iṣẹ́ ìṣẹ̀ǹbáyé wọn dúró, wọ́n sì ń wo ojú ọ̀run pẹ̀lú ìjayà, nítorí ìjì líle kan ń bọ̀ wá.' Kini akori akọkọ ti a le ri ninu ẹsẹ yi?
options: Iyipada ojú ọjọ́ ati ẹ̀rù ti o dá sí awọn àgbẹ̀
Itan iṣowo laarin awọn ilu meji
questions.explanation: The passage centres on a sudden change in weather in Ijẹbu and the resulting fear among farmers who abandon their work upon seeing signs of an approaching storm.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Lati inu ẹsẹ kanna, kini a le ka lati inu ọrọ 'ìjayà' gẹgẹ bi a ti lo o ninu gbolohun naa?
questions.explanation: In context, 'ìjayà' refers to a feeling of fear or apprehension, matching how the farmers react anxiously to the sky as the storm approaches.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Da lori ẹsẹ kanna, kini a le ṣe amoro rẹ (infer) nipa ipo awọn àgbẹ̀ naa laisi ki a ka a ni gbangba ninu ẹsẹ naa?
options: Won yoo tesiwaju iṣẹ won lai fiyesi ojú ọjọ́
Won le pinnu lati wa ààbò tabi ibi ààbò nitori iberu ìjì to ń bọ̀
Won ti pinnu lati kuro ni oko fun ààyè
Ẹsẹ naa ko fun wa ni alaye kankan lati fi ṣe amoro
questions.explanation: Although not explicitly stated, the description of farmers halting work and watching the sky with fear implies they are likely to seek shelter or safety before the storm arrives — an inference drawn from contextual clues.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Bi a se n tumọ gbolohun Gẹẹsi 'The chief priest consulted the oracle before the coronation' si ede Yoruba, ewo ninu awọn wọnyi ni ogbufo to peye julọ?
options: Olori àlùfáà náà bá awọn ọmọ ìjọ sọ̀rọ̀ ṣáájú ayẹyẹ
Babaláwo náà bèèrè Ifá ṣáájú ìsipa oyè náà
Olú-àlùfáà náà rí ọ̀run ṣáájú ìgbéyàwó
Ọba náà kọ orin ṣáájú ìsipa oyè náà
questions.explanation: 'Babaláwo náà bèèrè Ifá ṣáájú ìsipa oyè náà' accurately conveys the meaning of consulting a diviner (Ifa oracle) before a coronation, preserving both meaning and correct Yoruba grammatical structure.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ewo ninu awọn ogbufo wọnyi ti oro Gẹẹsi 'It is better to prevent than to cure' ṣe deede julọ ni ede Yoruba, ni lilo owe kan ti o ba a mu?
options: Bi a ba nṣe egbogi a ma n gbadun rẹ̀
Ìṣọ́ra kàn kò lè pa ọ̀tá
Àìsàn kì í kú láìsí egbò
questions.explanation: 'Ìdènà san ju ìwòsàn lọ' is a direct and grammatically natural Yoruba equivalent of the English saying 'prevention is better than cure,' correctly capturing both meaning and idiomatic structure.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini iṣoro ti o wọpọ julọ nigba ti a ba ṣe ogbufo ọrọ Gẹẹsi kan lọ si Yoruba ni ọna 'ọrọ-fun-ọrọ' (word-for-word)?
options: Ko si iṣoro kankan, o dara ju gbogbo ọna miran lọ
Gbolohun to jade le ma ni oye ninu Yoruba tabi ki o ya kuro ninu ilana girama Yoruba to peye
Ọna yi n mu ki ogbufo yara ju bi o ti ye lọ
Ọna yi ni JAMB nikan n gba fun gbogbo idahun
questions.explanation: Literal word-for-word translation often fails to preserve natural sentence flow and can violate the target language's own grammatical rules, producing translations that sound unnatural or unclear in Yoruba.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ninu idanwo Akaye, ewo ninu awọn ilana wọnyi ni yoo ran akẹkọ lọwọ julọ lati dahun ibeere ti n beere 'kini idi ti onkọwe fi lo ọrọ yi'?
options: Ki o wo bi ọrọ naa ṣe n ṣiṣẹ ninu ọrọ-ọrọ (context) ẹsẹ naa ati ipa ti o n ṣe si itumọ gbogbo rẹ̀
Ki o kan wo iwe atumọ ede Gẹẹsi laisi ero si ẹsẹ naa
Ki o fojufo ọrọ naa patapata ki o si dahun bi o se fẹ
Ki o ka ẹsẹ naa lekan kan soso lai pada wo o mọ
questions.explanation: Understanding an author's word choice requires examining how that word functions contextually within the passage and what effect it has on overall meaning, not relying on isolated dictionary definitions.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ẹsẹ ìwòye tí a ń kọ láti fi hàn ìmọ̀lára jíjinlẹ̀ àti láti lo àwòrán (imagery) ju bí a ti ń rí i ninu ẹsẹ arọ (prose) lasan?
questions.explanation: Poetic passages (ẹsẹ ẹwì) are characterised by deeper emotional expression and rich figurative imagery, distinguishing them from ordinary prose passages which tend toward straightforward narration.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe Ìjálá ninu Litereso Alenu Yoruba?
options: Orin ìsìnkú tí àwọn obìnrin ń kọ
Ẹsẹ orin/ewi ìṣọdẹ tí àwọn ọdẹ ń kọ láti yin Ògún àti ẹranko igbó
Ere ìbéèrè àti ìdáhùn àwọn ọmọdé
Owe tí a ń lò ní ìgbéyàwó
questions.explanation: Ìjálá is a distinct oral poetic chant traditionally performed by hunters, closely associated with the worship of Ògún, celebrating hunting exploits and the forest world.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini iyato akọkọ laarin Ìjálá ati Rárà gẹgẹ bi awọn oriṣi ewi alenu ninu asa Yoruba?
options: Ìjálá jẹ́ ewì àwọn ọdẹ tí ó ní ìsopọ̀ pẹ̀lú Ògún, Rárà sì jẹ́ oríṣi ẹ̀wì tí a ń fi yin ẹnikẹ́ni tàbí ṣe àpèjúwe ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ ní èdè tí ó gbé sókè
Awọn mejeeji jẹ́ ohun kan náà ní gbogbo ọ̀nà
Rárà nìkan ni àwọn ọdẹ ń kọ
Ìjálá kò ní í ṣe pẹ̀lú orin rárá
questions.explanation: While both are chanted oral poetry forms, Ìjálá is specifically tied to hunters and Ògún worship, whereas Rárà is a more general praise-chant form used to eulogise individuals or narrate events in an elevated poetic style.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe Ẹṣà ninu ewi alenu Yoruba, ti a maa n so mọ awọn egúngún?
options: Ẹsẹ ìyìn tí àwọn Ẹgbẹ́ Ẹgúngún ń kọ nígbà ìjó egúngún
Ọ̀rọ̀ ìjìnlẹ̀ tí babaláwo ń lò nínú Ifá
Owe tí a ń lò ní ilé ìwòsàn
Ẹsẹ tí àwọn ọdẹ ń kọ nínú igbó
questions.explanation: Ẹ̀sà refers to a chant or praise poetry associated with masquerade (Egúngún) performances, distinct from Ìjálá (hunters' chant) or Ifá poetry.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ewo ninu awọn wọnyi ṣe apejuwe iyato pataki laarin Ìjálá, Ẹṣà, ati Rárà gẹgẹ bi awọn oriṣi ewi alenu?
options: Won je ohun kanna, orukọ nikan ni o yato laarin awọn agbegbe
Won ko ni ibatan kankan pẹlu ara won rara
Won ya sọtọ nipa ẹgbẹ awujọ tabi ayeye ti won ṣe pataki si — Ìjálá fun ọdẹ, Ẹṣà fun egúngún, Rárà fun iyin gbogboogbo
Ìjálá àti Ẹṣà nìkan ni a lè kọ láìsí ìlù
questions.explanation: Each of these oral poetry genres is tied to a distinct social or ceremonial context: Ìjálá to hunters, Ẹṣà to masquerade performances, and Rárà to general praise chanting, though all fall under Yoruba oral literature.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ẹsẹ tí babaláwo ń ké nígbà tí ó bá ń ṣí Ifá payá fún onibáárà rẹ̀?
questions.explanation: Ẹsẹ Ifá refers to the sacred verses chanted by a Babalawo when interpreting the Ifa divination system for a client, forming an extensive body of oral literary and philosophical tradition.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe alọ ti idahun rẹ le yato lati eniyan kan si eniyan miran, tabi ti ko ni idahun kan soso ti a gba mọ (Alọ Apamọ)?
options: Alọ tí ó ní ìdáhùn kan tí gbogbo ènìyàn gbà
Alọ Apamọ, tí ó máa ń fi ọgbọ́n hàn ju ìdáhùn gidi lọ
questions.explanation: Alọ Apamọ are riddles whose answers are less fixed and more open to clever, imaginative interpretation, emphasising wit and reasoning over recalling one 'correct' factual answer.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe Alọ Apatagbe ninu asa Yoruba, ti a fi we Alọ Apamọ?
options: Alọ tí ó jẹ́ ìtàn gígùn tí ó ní ìhùwàsí àti àwọn ohun kikọ, tí a ń pè ní ìtàn àlọ́
Alọ tí kò ní ìtàn kankan rárá
Owe tí a ń lò ní ọjà
Oríkì tí a ń kọ fún ọba
questions.explanation: Alọ Apatagbe refers to full folktale narratives with plot, characters, and moral lessons (ìtàn àlọ́), distinguished from Alọ Apamọ, which are short riddle-style question-and-answer exchanges.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ewo ninu awọn wọnyi ni apẹẹrẹ tí ó tọ́ jùlọ fún Alọ Apatagbe, kii ṣe Alọ Apamọ?
options: 'Kín ni ó ń rìn láìní ẹsẹ̀?' pẹ̀lú ìdáhùn 'Odò'
Ìtàn ìjàkadì tó wà láàrin Ìjàpá àti Erin, tí ó parí pẹ̀lú ẹ̀kọ́ ìwà rere
'Ilé mi kún fún ọmọ, síbẹ̀ ẹnu-ọ̀nà kan ṣoṣo ni ó ní' pẹ̀lú ìdáhùn 'Kòkòrò oyin'
'Kín ni a ó rí tí a bá wo sánmà ní ọ̀sán?' pẹ̀lú ìdáhùn 'Oòrùn'
questions.explanation: The story of a contest between the Tortoise (Ìjàpá) and the Elephant, ending with a moral lesson, exemplifies Alọ Apatagbe — a full folktale with characters and plot — unlike the short riddle-style examples in the other options, which are Alọ Apamọ.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini idi ti Ìjàpá (Tortoise) ṣe wọpọ gẹgẹ bi ohun kikọ akọkọ ninu ọpọlọpọ Alọ Apatagbe Yoruba?
options: Nitori Ìjàpá je ẹranko to lagbara julọ ninu itan
Nitori Ìjàpá maa n ṣe afihan ọgbọn ẹ̀wẹ́ àti ẹ̀tàn, tí ó sábà máa ń kọ́ni ní ẹ̀kọ́ nípa ìwà rere àti àbájáde ìwà búburú
Nitori Ìjàpá kò lè sọ̀rọ̀ rárá nínú àwọn ìtàn wọnyi
Nitori Ìjàpá jẹ́ irú ẹyẹ kan
questions.explanation: The Tortoise is a recurring trickster character in Yoruba folktales, often portrayed using cunning and deceit, with stories typically illustrating moral consequences of such behaviour to teach ethical lessons.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini ipa ti orin tabi ilu n ṣe ninu bi a ṣe n ṣe Ìjálá ati Ẹṣà ninu iṣẹ won?
options: Won ko ni ibatan kankan pẹlu orin tabi ilu
Won máa ń fi ohùn kan ṣoṣo ké láìsí ìlù rárá
Won máa ń lo àyíká ohùn àti fífọn kìjà pàápàá bí kò sí ìlù, ní ọ̀nà tí ó yàtọ̀ sí orin lásán
Won máa ń kọrin bí orin ìjó gbajúmọ̀ nìkan
questions.explanation: Both Ìjálá and Ẹṣà are chanted using distinctive vocal patterns and stylised intonation, often without conventional musical accompaniment, marking them apart from ordinary popular songs.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe apa ninu Alọ Apatagbe ti n fun ni ẹkọ iwa rere ni ipari itan naa?
questions.explanation: Most Yoruba folktales conclude with a clear moral lesson (ẹ̀kọ́ ìwà), teaching the listener about proper conduct through the outcome of the story's events.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a n pe ohun ìjìnlẹ̀ inú ewi Ifá tí ó jẹ́ kí ó yàtọ̀ sí ewi lásán, ní pé ó ní ìsopọ̀ pẹ̀lú ìmọ̀ ìjìnlẹ̀ àti ìtàn àtọwọ́dọ́wọ́?
options: Ẹsẹ Ifá ní ìsopọ̀ pẹ̀lú ẹ̀kọ́ ìṣèlú òde-òní nìkan
Ẹsẹ Ifá kò ní ìtumọ̀ jíjinlẹ̀ kankan
Ẹsẹ Ifá gbé ìmọ̀ ìjìnlẹ̀, ìtàn, àti ìlànà ìwà rere tí a ti ń fi ẹnu sọ láti ìran dé ìran jáde
Ẹsẹ Ifá jẹ́ ewì tí a ṣẹ̀ṣẹ̀ dá láìpẹ́
questions.explanation: Ifa verses carry deep philosophical, historical, and moral knowledge that has been orally transmitted across generations, making Ifa poetry a rich repository of traditional Yoruba wisdom rather than mere entertainment verse.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ipele ninu Alọ Apamọ nibi ti eniyan meji ba n paarọ ọrọ ìsáájú kí ìbéèrè tó bẹ̀rẹ̀, gẹ́gẹ́ bí 'Àlọ́ o!' àti ìdáhùn 'Àlọ́!'?
options: Ìpè àti ìdáhùn ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ (opening call-and-response formula)
questions.explanation: Yoruba riddle sessions traditionally begin with a fixed call-and-response formula between the riddler and the audience, signalling the start of the riddling exchange before the actual riddle is posed.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini idi ti Rárà fi le ni ibatan pẹlu iyin oba, oloye, ati eniyan pataki, yato si Ìjálá tabi Ẹṣà?
options: Nitori Rárà je ti ile-iwosan nikan
Nitori Rárà kò ní ìbáṣepọ̀ pẹ̀lú ẹnikẹ́ni
Nitori Rárà jẹ́ oríṣi ẹ̀wì gbogbo-gbòò tí a lè ṣàtúnṣe rẹ̀ láti yin ẹnikẹ́ni tàbí ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀, kì í ṣe ẹgbẹ́ kan pàtó
Nitori Rárà jẹ́ ohun kan náà pẹ̀lú owe
questions.explanation: Unlike Ìjálá (specific to hunters) or Ẹṣà (specific to masquerades), Rárà is a flexible praise-chant form that can be adapted to eulogise kings, chiefs, or any notable individual or event.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ka gbolohun yi: 'Bí a bá bọ́ ọmọdé lẹ́nu iṣẹ́, a kì í fi í sí ọwọ́ ìdàrọ́.' Kini itumọ jinlẹ ti owe yi n gbiyanju lati fi han?
options: Ki a ma fi ọmọdé sisẹ patapata
Bi a ba fi ẹnikan ni ominira kuro ninu ojuse kan, ki a ma fi i sinu ewu miran tí ó le burú jù
Àwọn àgbà ni ó gbọ́dọ̀ ṣiṣẹ́ nìkan
questions.explanation: This proverb warns that if a child (or anyone) is relieved from one form of hardship or responsibility, care must be taken not to place them into an even more dangerous or harmful situation.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Nínú ìtúpalẹ̀ eré-oníṣé (drama) lédè Yorùbá, kí ni a ń pè ọ̀rọ̀ tí ohun kikọ kan sọ fún ara rẹ̀ nìkan lórí ìtàgé, láìsí kí àwọn ohun kikọ mìíràn gbọ́ ọ (aside/soliloquy)?
questions.explanation: A soliloquy or aside (ọ̀rọ̀-inú) allows a character to reveal inner thoughts directly to the audience, unheard by other characters on stage, a key dramatic technique distinct from ordinary dialogue.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ohun kikọ ninu itan tabi eré ti n koju ohun kikọ akọkọ (protagonist) ti o si n dá ìṣòro sílẹ̀ fún un?
questions.explanation: The antagonist is the character who opposes the main character (protagonist) and creates the central conflict that drives the plot forward.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ìlànà tí a fi ń gbé ìtàn kalẹ̀ láti ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ dé òpin, tí ó ní ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ tí ó so ara wọn pọ̀ ní ọ̀wọ̀ọ̀wọ́ kan (plot)?
questions.explanation: The plot (ìtàn-àròsọ) refers to the structured sequence of connected events that make up the narrative arc of a literary work, from introduction through climax to resolution.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ninu itupale itan aroso Yoruba, kini iyato laarin 'akori' (theme) ati 'ẹ̀kọ́ ìwà' (moral lesson) ti iwe kan?
options: Akori ni ero pataki gbogbogbo ti onkọwe fẹ fi han, nigba ti ẹkọ iwa ni ẹ̀kọ́ pàtó tí a ń rí gbà nípa ìwà rere láti inú ìtàn náà
Akori àti ẹ̀kọ́ ìwà jẹ́ ohun kan náà ní gbogbo ìgbà
Akori kì í fi ara hàn nínú ewi rárá
Ẹ̀kọ́ ìwà jẹ́ orúkọ ìwé nìkan
questions.explanation: The theme is the broad central idea or subject matter of a work, while the moral lesson is a specific ethical takeaway about proper conduct that readers can extract from how the story unfolds.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ipò àti àkókò tí ìtàn kan bá wáyé, gẹ́gẹ́ bí ìlú kan ní ọ̀rúndún kẹtàdínlógún ninu itan aroso Yoruba?
questions.explanation: The setting (àyíká-ọ̀rọ̀) refers to the place and time in which the events of a story occur, an essential element for understanding the context of a written literary work.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ilana ninu eyi ti onkọwe kan n lo ohun kikọ lati fi kọlu iwa buburu kan ninu awujọ nipasẹ awada tabi yẹyẹ (satire)?
questions.explanation: Satire (ẹ̀gàn-àwùjọ) is a literary technique used to criticise societal vices or human folly through humour, irony, or exaggeration, often carrying a serious underlying message.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Nínú eré-oníṣé Yorùbá, kí ni a ń pè ìpín inú eré tí a fi ń yà á sọ́tọ̀ọ̀tọ̀ fún ìtẹ̀síwájú ìtàn, gẹ́gẹ́ bí 'Ìṣe Kìíní'?
questions.explanation: A play is typically divided into acts (ìṣe), major structural divisions that organise the progression of the dramatic story, often further split into scenes.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ohun kikọ ti kò yí padà ní ìwà jákèjádò ìtàn kan, tí ó dúró ṣinṣin nínú ìwà rẹ̀ láti ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ dé òpin (static/flat character)?
questions.explanation: A static or flat character remains largely unchanged in personality or outlook throughout a narrative, in contrast to a dynamic character who undergoes significant development or transformation.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kí ni a lè kà sí àbùkù (weakness/flaw) pàtàkì nínú ohun kikọ àkọ́kọ́ (tragic flaw) tí ó máa ń yọrí sí ìṣubú rẹ̀ nínú eré ìbànújẹ́ (tragedy)?
options: Ìwà rere tí kò ní àbùkù kankan
Àìsàn tí ó dé bá ẹnikẹ́ni lásán
Àbùkù inú ìwà (tragic flaw) tí ó fa ìṣubú ẹ̀mí ohun kikọ náà
questions.explanation: A tragic flaw is an inherent character weakness — such as excessive pride or ambition — that ultimately leads to the protagonist's downfall in a tragedy, a key concept in dramatic literary analysis.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe isọmọloruko ninu asa Yoruba?
options: Ayẹyẹ ti a n ṣe lati fun ọmọ tuntun ni orukọ
questions.explanation: Ìsọmọlóruko is the traditional Yoruba naming ceremony held to formally give a newborn child a name, usually performed within the first seven to nine days after birth.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ni deede, ni ọjọ melo lẹhin ibi ọmọ ni a maa n ṣe ayẹyẹ isọmọloruko fun ọmọkunrin ninu asa Yoruba ibile?
questions.explanation: Traditionally, the Yoruba naming ceremony for a baby boy is held on the ninth day after birth, while for a baby girl it is commonly held on the seventh day, reflecting customary practice (though this varies by locality).

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe eyin ọbẹ, oyin, ati omi ti a maa n lo lakoko isọmọloruko lati fi júwe iru ọjọ iwaju ti a n fẹ fun ọmọ naa?
questions.explanation: Various symbolic items such as honey, water, kola nut, and salt are used during the naming ceremony, each representing a wish or blessing for a particular quality in the child's future life.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ilana ninu eyi ti idile ọkọ n mu ẹbun wa si idile iyawo lati beere fun ọwọ ọmọbinrin won ninu asa igbeyawo Yoruba?
questions.explanation: Ìdána refers to the traditional introduction and bride-price stage of Yoruba marriage customs, during which the groom's family formally presents gifts to the bride's family to seek her hand in marriage.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ninu igbeyawo ibile Yoruba, kini ipa ti 'Alaga Ìjọ' n ṣe ninu ayẹyẹ naa?
options: O n ṣe amona/olutọju ilana ayẹyẹ, ti n ṣakoso bi ayẹyẹ ṣe n lọ
O n ṣe onje fun awọn alejo
O n kọrin nikan jakejado ayẹyẹ
questions.explanation: The Alaga Ìjọ (mistress/master of ceremonies on the bride's side) coordinates and moderates the wedding ceremony, guiding the proceedings and often adding entertainment through witty remarks.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe iṣesi ninu eyi ti iyawo n te siwaju ni ese lati juwe iteriba fun awọn obi ọkọ ati alejo lakoko igbeyawo ibile Yoruba?
questions.explanation: Prostration or kneeling (ìdòbálẹ̀ for men, ìkúnlẹ̀ for women) is a traditional gesture of respect performed during ceremonies such as weddings, reflecting deep-rooted Yoruba customs of greeting and deference to elders.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ewo ninu awọn wọnyi ṣe iyato laarin bi ọkunrin ati obinrin ṣe n ki agbalagba ni ibile Yoruba?
options: Awọn mejeeji a maa fi ọwọ kan ilẹ̀ nikan lai tẹriba
Ọkunrin a maa dọbalẹ (dà bọ̀ọ̀lẹ̀ pátápátá sí ilẹ̀), obinrin a sì maa kúnlẹ̀ (kneel) láti kí àgbà
Ọkunrin nikan ni o gbọdọ ki agbalagba
Obinrin nikan ni o gbọdọ ki agbalagba
questions.explanation: In traditional Yoruba greeting etiquette, men typically prostrate fully on the ground (ìdòbálẹ̀), while women kneel (ìkúnlẹ̀), both gestures expressing deep respect toward elders.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ilana isinku ti idile n ṣe lati bu ọla fun okú ẹni ti o ti darugbo daadaa ninu asa Yoruba, ti a n pe ni 'sisin oku sinu ayọ'?
options: Ìsìnkú Ayọ̀ (celebration-style funeral rite for an elder)
questions.explanation: When an elderly person who lived a full life passes away, Yoruba tradition often treats the funeral as a celebration of life, marked with festivity alongside mourning, distinct from the burial rites for a younger person.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe aṣọ pataki ti idile ma n wọ ni akoko isinku ninu asa Yoruba lati fi han iṣọkan ati ọfọ?
options: Aṣọ Aró/Aṣọ-Ìbílẹ̀ Ọ̀fọ̀ (mourning attire, often chosen in a matching family colour)
questions.explanation: Yoruba families often adopt a specific mourning attire — commonly in a chosen uniform colour — during funeral ceremonies to symbolise unity and shared grief among relatives.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ninu asa isinku Yoruba, kini a npe akoko ti a n ṣe ayẹyẹ iranti fun oku ni ọjọ kan, ọsẹ kan tabi osu kan lẹhin isinku?
questions.explanation: Ìrántí refers to memorial or remembrance rites held some time after burial to continue honouring the deceased, part of the broader set of Yoruba funeral customs.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini ikini 'Ẹ kú àárọ̀' ṣe túmọ̀ sí, tí a máa ń lò ní àkókò kan pàtó ọjọ́?
questions.explanation: 'Ẹ kú àárọ̀' is the traditional Yoruba morning greeting, one of several time-specific greetings used to acknowledge others appropriately throughout the day.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini ikini to yẹ ki a lo fun ẹnikan ti a ba ri ti n ṣiṣẹ takuntakun ninu asa ikini Yoruba?
options: Ẹ kú iṣẹ́ (well done/greetings on your work)
questions.explanation: 'Ẹ kú iṣẹ́' is the customary Yoruba greeting acknowledging and appreciating someone who is seen actively engaged in work or labour.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini idi to fi je ki ikini (ìkíni) ka si iye asa pataki ninu ẹgbẹ awujọ Yoruba, kii ṣe lasan wi 'kaabo' tabi 'e ku aaro'?
options: Nitori ikini ko ni itumọ awujọ eyikeyi
Nitori ikini n ṣàfihàn iteriba, ibasepọ, ati eto awujọ laarin awọn eniyan, gẹgẹ bi ọjọ ori ati ipo won
Nitori JAMB nikan n beere ibeere lori ikini
Nitori ikini je asa titun ti a ṣẹṣẹ da lode oni
questions.explanation: Greetings in Yoruba culture go beyond simple pleasantries; they express respect, social hierarchy, and relationship dynamics, reflecting deeply embedded social values around age and status.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini iyato laarin bi a se n ki ẹnikan ti o dagba ju wa lọ ati bi a se n ki ẹnikan ti o ba wa dọgba ni ọjọ ori ninu asa Yoruba?
options: Ko si iyato kankan ninu ọna ikini
A máa ń fi ọ̀wọ̀ hàn àti ìkúnlẹ̀/ìdòbálẹ̀ fún àgbà, nígbà tí a lè kí ẹgbẹ́ẹgbẹ́ ní ọ̀nà tí kò fi bẹ́ẹ̀ jinlẹ̀
A máa ń dọ̀bálẹ̀ fún ẹgbẹ́ẹgbẹ́ nìkan
Àwọn àgbà nìkan ni ó gbọ́dọ̀ kí àwọn ọ̀dọ́
questions.explanation: Greeting an elder typically involves more formal, deferential gestures such as kneeling or prostration, while greetings between age-mates tend to be more casual, reflecting the Yoruba social value placed on respecting seniority.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe orukọ amutorunwa (orukọ ti a gbagbọ pe ọmọ mu wa lati orun), gẹgẹ bi 'Tainiwo' tabi 'Ige'?
options: Orúkọ àbíso lásán tí kò ní ìtumọ̀ kankan
Orúkọ àmútọ̀runwá (name reflecting circumstances of birth believed destined from heaven)
questions.explanation: Orúkọ àmútọ̀runwá are special names given based on the unique circumstances surrounding a child's birth (such as being born feet-first, or as a twin), believed to reflect a destiny the child brought from the spiritual realm.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ibeji ninu asa Yoruba, ati kini pataki won ni asa ibile?
options: Ibeji je ọmọ meji ti a bi papọ, ti a si maa n ka si pataki, ti won sì ní òrìṣà kan pàtó tí a ń bọ fún wọn (Ìbejì)
Ibeji je ọrọ fun ọmọ kan soso
Ibeji je oruko fun ọmọ akọbi nikan
Ibeji ko ni pataki kankan ninu asa Yoruba
questions.explanation: Twins (ìbejì) hold special cultural and spiritual significance in Yoruba tradition, with a dedicated belief system and set of customs, including carved figures (ère ìbejì) made if a twin dies.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini ipa ti Ẹgbẹ́ Ọjọ́-orí (age-grade society) n ṣe ninu eto awujọ ibile Yoruba?
options: Ẹgbẹ́ Ọjọ́-orí ko ni ipa kankan ninu awujọ
Ó jẹ́ ẹgbẹ́ fún àwọn babaláwo nìkan
Ó jẹ́ ẹgbẹ́ tí a dá sílẹ̀ láìpẹ́ yìí láti ọwọ́ ìjọba
Ó máa ń ṣètò iṣẹ́ àwùjọ, ìdáàbòbò ìlú, àti ẹ̀kọ́ ìwà fún àwọn ọ̀dọ́ tí wọ́n bí ní àkókò kan náà
questions.explanation: Ẹgbẹ́ Ọjọ́-orí (age-grade associations) organised people born around the same period into groups responsible for communal labour, town defence, and instilling moral discipline in the young — a key traditional social institution distinct from religious or modern government bodies.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Alagbede ninu asa ibile Yoruba n ṣe amọdaju iru ise wo?
options: Alagbede n ṣiṣẹ irin, ti n dá ohun èlò iṣẹ́ àti ohun ìjà láti inú irin
Alagbede n hun aso lori owu
questions.explanation: Alágbède is the traditional blacksmith, working iron into tools, farm implements, and weapons — a specialised, often hereditary profession central to Yoruba craft-guild traditions.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini iyato akọkọ laarin Babaláwo ati Onísègùn ninu eto ilera ibile Yoruba?
options: Ko si iyato kankan, oro kanna ni awon mejeeji
Babaláwo àti Onísègùn jẹ́ orúkọ méjì fún oyè oba
Onísègùn nìkan ló ń lo ẹ̀kọ́ Ifá nínú iṣẹ́ rẹ̀
Babaláwo ń ṣiṣẹ́ Ifá àti àsọtẹ́lẹ̀ láti mọ ìdí ìṣòro, nígbà tí Onísègùn ń lo egbò àti egbogi láti wo àìsàn sàn
questions.explanation: A Babaláwo divines through Ifá to diagnose the spiritual cause of a problem, while an Onísègùn (traditional herbalist) treats ailments using herbal medicine — related but distinct roles within Yoruba traditional practice.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ninu igbagbo ibile Yoruba, kini ipo ti Olódùmarè ni idi ninu awon Òrìṣà bi Ṣàngó ati Ògún?
options: Olódùmarè jẹ́ Òrìṣà kan lára àwọn Òrìṣà yòókù, tí ó dọ́gba pẹ̀lú Ṣàngó
Olódùmarè jẹ́ Òrìṣà tí ó kéré jù nínú gbogbo àwọn Òrìṣà
Olódùmarè ni Ẹlẹ́dàá àgbáyé àti orísun agbára gbogbo Òrìṣà, ó sì ga ju gbogbo Òrìṣà lọ
Olódùmarè kò ní ìsopọ̀ kankan pẹ̀lú àwọn Òrìṣà
questions.explanation: In Yoruba cosmology, Olódùmarè is the Supreme Being, the ultimate creator and source of authority, while the òrìṣà (such as Ṣàngó, god of thunder, and Ògún, god of iron) are lesser divinities who serve as intermediaries between Olódùmarè and humanity.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini o ṣe iyato laarin Ṣàngó ati Ògún gẹgẹ bi Òrìṣà meji ninu igbagbo ibile Yoruba?
options: Ṣàngó àti Ògún jẹ́ Òrìṣà kan náà tí a ń pè ní orúkọ méjì
Ògún ni Òrìṣà àrá, Ṣàngó sì ni Òrìṣà irin
Kò sí Òrìṣà kankan tí à ń pè ní Ṣàngó nínú ìtàn Yorùbá
Ṣàngó ni Òrìṣà àrá àti mọ̀nàmọ́ná, tí a sì so mọ ọba Ọ̀yọ́ àtijọ́, nígbà tí Ògún ni Òrìṣà irin àti ogun, tí àwọn alágbède àti ọdẹ ń bọ
questions.explanation: Ṣàngó is the deity of thunder and lightning, linked to the ancient Ọ̀yọ́ monarchy, while Ògún is the deity of iron and war, worshipped especially by blacksmiths, hunters, and warriors — each with distinct domains despite both being major òrìṣà.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ijosin ti a n se fun awon baba nla ti o ti ku ninu asa Yoruba, ti a maa n fi Egúngún han ni gbangba?
options: Ìjọsìn Egúngún kò ní ìsopọ̀ pẹ̀lú àwọn baba ńlá tí ó ti kú rí
Egúngún jẹ́ oyè tí a ń fún àwọn oyè ìlú nìkan
Egúngún jẹ́ orúkọ mìíràn fún ère ìbejì
Ìjọsìn Egúngún jẹ́ ọ̀nà tí à ń gbà bu ọlá fún àwọn baba ńlá tí ó ti kú, tí a gbà gbọ́ pé wọ́n padà wá bẹ̀ àwọn ẹbí wọn wò
questions.explanation: The Egúngún masquerade tradition is an ancestor-veneration practice — masked figures are believed to embody the spirits of departed forebears returning to bless, admonish, or commune with their living descendants.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ninu fonoloji Yoruba, iru sílébù wo ni o wọpọ julọ, gẹgẹ bi a ṣe rii ninu 'ba', 'kọ', ati 'ṣe'?
options: Kọnsonanti-Faweli (KF), níbi tí kọ́nsonáǹtì kan ti tẹ̀lé e pẹ̀lú fáwélì kan
questions.explanation: The dominant syllable structure in Yoruba is Consonant + Vowel (CV) — every syllable typically ends in a vowel (or is a syllabic nasal), as seen in 'ba', 'kọ', 'ṣe'.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ohun (tone) mẹta wo ni a mọ ninu ede Yoruba, ti a fi n ṣe iyato itumọ oro bi 'igba' (200, ọgba, akoko)?
options: Ohun kan soso ni ede Yoruba ni
Ohun-ga ati ohun-kekere nikan, laisi ohun-arin
Ohun mẹrin: ga, arin, kekere, ati aarin-arin
questions.explanation: Standard Yoruba has three level tones — high (dòjú/ré, marked ´), mid (unmarked), and low (marked `) — whose combinations distinguish words like 'igbá' (calabash), 'ìgbà' (time/rope), and 'ìgba' (two hundred).

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe iṣupọ konsonanti pataki bi 'gb' ati 'kp' ninu ede Yoruba, ti a ko le pin si kọnsonanti meji lọtọ ni pipe?
options: A npe won ni faweli imu
A npe won ni sile alaimoye
A npe won ni digrafu tabi kọnsonanti alapọ, ti a n pe bi ohun kan soso botilẹjẹ pe wọn ni ami kikọ meji
questions.explanation: 'Gb' (and historically 'kp') is a co-articulated labio-velar stop written with two letters but pronounced as a single consonant sound — a digraph, not a true consonant cluster, in Yoruba phonology.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ninu isodipupo oro Yoruba, kini a npe ilana ninu eyi ti oro kan ba tun ara re se ni odindi tabi ni apa kan lati fi kun itumo, gege bi 'yara-yara' lati inu 'yara' (fi han kiakia)?
questions.explanation: Reduplication (ìlọ́pọ̀-méjì) — repeating a word or stem, as in 'yara-yara' (quickly) from 'yara' (fast/room) — is a productive morphological process in Yoruba used to intensify or modify meaning.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe iru oro-orukọ ti a da nipa fifi ìránṣé 'a-' kun oro-ise kan, gẹgẹ bi 'akọrin' (singer) lati inu 'ko orin' (sings a song)?
options: Ọ̀rọ̀-orúkọ tí a dá nípa ìránṣé àṣàájú-ọ̀rọ̀ (agentive prefix 'a-') tí a fi kún gbòǹgbò ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe láti dá orúkọ tí ó ń tọ́ka sí ẹni tí ó ń ṣe iṣẹ́ náà
Ọ̀rọ̀-orúkọ àpapọ̀ (compound noun) laisi eyikeyi ìránṣé
Ọ̀rọ̀-ìse tí kò yí padà rárá
Ọ̀rọ̀ ìdìde tí kò ní ìtumọ̀ kankan
questions.explanation: Prefixing 'a-' to a verb phrase forms an agentive noun denoting 'one who does X' — e.g. 'akọrin' (a singer, one who sings a song) from 'ko orin' — a common derivational morphology pattern in Yoruba.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ilana ninu eyi ti faweli kan ninu oro kan gbọdọ baamu iru faweli miran ti o wa nitosi re fun ki ohun ọrọ naa le da (vowel harmony), paapa julọ ninu awon iselu ATR ninu ede Yoruba?
options: Ìsúnkì fáwélì, níbi tí fáwélì kan ti pòórá pátápátá
Ìdàpọ̀ kọ́nsonáǹtì, níbi tí kọ́nsonáǹtì méjì ti di ọ̀kan
Ìyípadà ohùn láti orí sí ìsàlẹ̀ láìsí ìdí kankan
Ìfohùnṣọ̀kan fáwélì, níbi tí fáwélì kan gbọ́dọ̀ bá fáwélì mìíràn mu ní ìhà ìdí ahọ́n (ATR) láàrin gbòǹgbò ọ̀rọ̀ àti ìránṣé rẹ̀
questions.explanation: Vowel harmony in Yoruba requires vowels within certain morpheme sequences to agree in the tongue-root feature (ATR — advanced vs. non-advanced tongue root), which governs how prefixes and roots co-occur phonologically.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini o mu ki Ìjálá ni ibatan pataki pẹlu Ògún, Òrìṣà irin ati ọdẹ, ju bi Ẹṣà tabi Rárà se ri?
options: Ìjálá kò ní ìsopọ̀ kankan pẹ̀lú Ògún
Ìjálá jẹ́ ewì tí a ń kọ fún ìsìnkú nìkan
Ẹṣà ni ewì tí a fi ń yin Ògún, kìí ṣe Ìjálá
Ìjálá ni ewì tí àwọn ọdẹ àti àwọn olùjọsìn Ògún ń kọ láti yin akikanju, ohun ọdẹ, àti ìṣẹ́gun, tí ó sì ní èdè àti àkànṣe ọ̀rọ̀ tirẹ̀
questions.explanation: Ìjálá is chiefly a hunters' chant tradition associated with Ògún, celebrating bravery, hunting exploits, and heroism, with its own distinctive diction and cadence, distinguishing it from Ẹṣà (linked to egúngún) and Rárà (linked to praise of royalty).

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe akojo ese ti Babalawo n lo ninu Ifa lati salaye idi kan pato ti a fi ye onibaara kan, ti o si maa n ni ìtàn àti òwe ninu?
options: Rárà, tí a fi ń yin ọba nìkan
Àlọ́ Apamọ, tí kò ní ìsopọ̀ kankan pẹ̀lú Ifá
