Odù Ifá, tí ó jẹ́ àkójọ ẹsẹ tí ó ní ìtàn, òwe, àti ìlànà ìwà nínú tí a fi ń tọ́ni sọ́nà
Oríkì, tí a fi ń pe orúkọ ìdílé nìkan
questions.explanation: An Odù Ifá is a body of divination verses recited by a Babaláwo, containing narratives, proverbs, and moral guidance used to address a client's specific concern — the core textual corpus of Ifá literature.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ohun kikọ ninu itan tabi eré ti iwa re yipada ni pataki bi itan naa se n lo (yato si ohun kikọ aiyipada)?
options: A npe iru ohun kikọ bayii ni ohun kikọ alayipada tabi alaraadi (round/dynamic character), ti idagbasoke re maa n je pataki ninu akori itan
A npe iru ohun kikọ bayii ni ohun kikọ aiyipada (static character)
A npe iru ohun kikọ bayii ni oluṣàkóso (narrator) nikan
A npe iru ohun kikọ bayii ni afokansi (antagonist) nikan
questions.explanation: A round/dynamic character undergoes meaningful change in personality, belief, or attitude over the course of a narrative, in contrast to a static (flat) character who remains essentially unchanged.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ewo ninu awọn wọnyi ṣe apejuwe ijaya-laarin-eniyan-ati-awujọ (man versus society) gẹgẹ bi iru ijaya (conflict) ninu itan tabi eré Yoruba?
options: Nigba ti akọni ba tako awon ofin tabi ilana ti awujọ gbogbo gba, ti o si ba won ja fun eto rẹ̀
Nigba ti akọni ba ja ogun pẹlu ara rẹ̀ nikan, ninu ọkan rẹ̀
Nigba ti eniyan meji ba ja ara won lasan fun ohun-ini
Nigba ti akọni ba ja pelu iji tabi ojo lasan
questions.explanation: Man-versus-society conflict occurs when a protagonist opposes prevailing societal norms, laws, or expectations — distinct from internal conflict (man vs. self), interpersonal conflict (man vs. man), or man vs. nature.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe iru olusoju-itan (narrator) ti o mo ero-inu ati itan gbogbo ohun kikọ ninu iwe kan, ko si si ohun ti o pamọ fun un?
options: Olùṣàkóso tí kò lè sọ ìtàn kankan
Olùṣàkóso tí ó jẹ́ ọ̀tá àkọ́kọ́ nínú ìtàn
Olùṣàkóso mọ̀-gbogbo-nǹkan (omniscient narrator), tí ó mọ ìrònú inú àti ìtàn ẹ̀yìn gbogbo ohun kíkọ
questions.explanation: An omniscient narrator has unrestricted knowledge of all characters' thoughts, motives, and backstories, unlike a first-person or limited narrator whose perspective is confined to one character's viewpoint.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ilana ninu eyi ti onkọwe kan ba ta ìtọ́kasí kékeré nípa ohun tí yóò ṣẹlẹ̀ nígbèyìn ìtàn, kí ó tó ṣẹlẹ̀ ní gidi?
options: A npe eyi ni àsọtẹ́lẹ̀-ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ tàbí àṣàsọtẹ́lẹ̀ (foreshadowing), tí ó máa ń fún òǹkàwé ní ìjápọ̀ ohun tí ń bọ̀
questions.explanation: Foreshadowing (àṣàsọtẹ́lẹ̀) is a literary device in which an author drops subtle hints about events that will occur later in the narrative, building anticipation without revealing the outcome outright.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ninu itupale itan aroso, kini pataki ipo (setting) itan kan, paapa nigba ti a ba lo abuleko ibile bi ipo itan naa?
options: Ipo itan (setting) le ṣe iranlọwọ lati fi han asa, igbagbọ, ati awọn iye ti o ni ipa lori iwa ati ipinnu awọn ohun kikọ ninu itan naa
Ipo itan ko ni ipa kankan lori itumọ tabi akori itan naa
Ipo itan wulo nikan fun sisọ akoko ti itan naa se sele
Ipo itan ati akori itan je oro kanna
questions.explanation: Setting does more than mark time and place — a traditional Yoruba village backdrop, for instance, can foreground cultural values, beliefs, and social pressures that directly shape characters' choices and the story's themes.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ka ẹsẹ yi: 'Àwọn ọmọ ìlú kó ra jọ ní gbọ̀ngàn ìjọba, wọ́n ń fojú sọ́nà de ọ̀rọ̀ tí baálé ìlú yóò sọ. Ìjì àìnírètí ti bo ojú ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀, nítorí oyà ti gbóná janjan ní ọdún yìí.' Kini akọ-ero (main idea) ninu ẹsẹ yi, yato si awọn oro-alaye (supporting details) bi ibi ipade ati idi ti won fi ni ireti?
options: Akọ-ero ni pe àwọn ọmọ ìlú kó jọ ní gbọ̀ngàn kan pàtó
Akọ-ero ni pe oyà ti gbóná janjan ní gbogbo àgbáyé
Akọ-ero ni pe àwọn aráàlú ń retí ìròyìn pàtàkì lọ́wọ́ olórí wọn láàárín àkókò ìnira ọrọ̀-ajé
Akọ-ero ni pe baálé ìlú kò lè sọ ọ̀rọ̀ kankan mọ́
questions.explanation: The main idea is the passage's central point — the townspeople anxiously awaiting their leader's word amid economic hardship — while details like the venue and the cause of anxiety merely support and illustrate that central idea.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini iṣoro pataki ti o le waye nigba ti a ba tumọ gbolohun-idiomu (idiomatic expression) Gẹẹsi bi 'to kick the bucket' ni ọna ọrọ-fun-ọrọ (literal) si Yoruba?
options: Kò sí ìṣòro kankan, gbogbo gbólóhùn ni a lè tú ní ọ̀rọ̀-fún-ọ̀rọ̀ láìsí ìyọnu
Ìtumọ̀ ọ̀rọ̀-fún-ọ̀rọ̀ máa ń mú ìtumọ̀ tí ó túbọ̀ jinlẹ̀ jáde ju ti Gẹ̀ẹ́sì lọ
Àwọn gbólóhùn ìdíọ̀mù kò ní ìtumọ̀ kankan rárá ní èdè èyíkéyìí
Ìtumọ̀ ọ̀rọ̀-fún-ọ̀rọ̀ lè pàdánù ìtumọ̀ àkọ́kọ́ tí gbólóhùn náà ní (láti kú), tí ó sì lè yọrí sí ìtumọ̀ tí kò bọ́gbọ́n mu tàbí tí ó yàtọ̀ pátápátá ní èdè Yorùbá
questions.explanation: Idioms carry figurative meaning that a literal, word-for-word translation destroys — translating 'kick the bucket' literally into Yoruba would produce a nonsensical or misleading rendering instead of conveying 'to die'.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Ewo ninu awọn wọnyi ṣe apẹẹrẹ Alọ Apamọ tí ó peye, ti a fi n bere ibeere ti idahun re yato si ero elomiran, yato si Alọ Apatagbe ti o ni itan gigun?
options: Itan gigun nipa bi Ijapa se tan Erin je pelu ẹkọ iwa ninu
Oriki gigun ti a fi n yin idile oba kan
Ijala ti odẹ kan n ko fun Ogun
'Ẹ̀kún dúdú lóde, funfun nínú - kí ni?' pẹ̀lú ìdáhùn tí ó lè yàtọ̀ (bí i agbọ̀n tàbí ohun mìíràn tí ó bá ìjuwe mu)
questions.explanation: Alọ Apamọ (riddles) pose a short descriptive puzzle whose answer can admit more than one plausible response based on the clues given, unlike Alọ Apatagbe, which is an extended narrative folktale with a fixed plot and explicit moral.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe ewi ti a n ko lati yin oruko, iwa, ati itan idile eniyan tabi ilu kan pato ninu asa Yoruba, ti o yato si Ijala tabi Rara ni bi a ti n lo o?
options: Oríkì, ewì ìdánimọ̀ tí a fi ń pe orúkọ, ìran, àti ìwà ẹnì kan tàbí ìdílé kan pàtó, tí a sì lè lò ní ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ààrọ̀ (ìbí, ìgbéyàwó, àti bẹ́ẹ̀ bẹ́ẹ̀ lọ)
Rárà, tí a fi ń yin ọba nìkan láìsí ìdílé kankan mìíràn
Ẹṣà, tí a fi ń fi hàn ìbínú sí àwọn ọ̀tá nìkan
Àlọ́ Apamọ, tí kò ní ìsopọ̀ kankan pẹ̀lú ìdánimọ̀ ẹnikẹ́ni
questions.explanation: Oríkì is a praise-chant tradition tied to a person's or lineage's identity, history, and attributes, usable across many occasions, distinguishing it from genre-specific chants like Ìjálá (hunters) or Rárà (royal praise).

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini iyato akọkọ laarin 'oruko amutorunwa' ati 'oruko abiso' ninu isọmọloruko ibile Yoruba?
options: Won je oro kanna, ko si iyato kankan
Oruko amutorunwa nikan ni a maa n fun awon obinrin
Oruko abiso nikan ni a maa n fi kọ omo silẹkọ ni ile-iwe

Oruko amutorunwa ni oruko ti a gba pe omo ti mu wa lati orun (bii ipo ibi rẹ̀, gẹgẹ bi Taiwo), nigba ti oruko abiso ni oruko ti awon obi tabi ẹbi n yan fun omo naa gege bi ipo idile tabi ohun ti n sele nigba ibi rẹ̀
questions.explanation: Orúkọ amútọ̀runwá are names believed to reflect the special circumstances of birth the child 'brought from heaven' (e.g. Táíwò, Àìná), while orúkọ àbíso are names deliberately chosen by the family based on family history, hopes, or events surrounding the birth.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini idi pataki fun 'idana' (bride price/dowry items) ninu igbeyawo ibile Yoruba?
options: Idana je san owo fun iyawo bi eru
Idana ko ni itumo kankan mọ ninu asa igbeyawo Yoruba
Idana je afihan ọwọ ati imoore ti idile ọkọ n fi han si idile iyawo, ati ami ifọwọsi ìdílé méjèèjì fún ìgbéyàwó náà
Idana je oro fun ile ti awon tọkọtaya yoo gbe
questions.explanation: Ìdána (bride-price items and gifts) is a symbolic gesture of respect and appreciation shown by the groom's family to the bride's family, and it formally seals both families' consent to the union — it is not a purchase transaction.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini a npe 'oku ayo' ninu asa isinku Yoruba, ti o yato si isinku deede ti kii se pelu ayo?
options: Oku ayo ni isinku ẹni tí ó kú lójijì ní ọ̀dọ̀ọ́rùn
Oku ayo ni orúkọ mìíràn fún isinku Egungun
Oku ayo je oro fun isinku awon oba nikan
Oku ayo ni isinku ẹni tí ó ti darúgbó dáadáa tí ó sì ní àwọn ọmọ àti ọmọ-ọmọ kí ó tó kú, tí a fi ń ṣe ayẹyẹ ìdùnnú dípò ẹkún
questions.explanation: 'Òkú ayọ̀' (a celebratory burial/funeral) is held for someone who died at a ripe old age with surviving children and grandchildren, celebrated with festivity rather than the mourning reserved for an untimely death ('òkú ẹkún').

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini oye ti a n fun Oba ni ilu Yoruba ni gbangba, ti o si maa n je apejuwe ipo re bi asoju Olodumare lori ile aye, ti a n pe ni 'Igbakeji Orisa'?
options: Oye yi tumo si wipe Oba je Olorisa lasan, ko si iyato kankan pelu awon Olorisa yoku
Oye yi je oruko fun awon omo oba nikan
Oye yi ko ni ipa kankan lori bi a se n bu ola fun Oba

Oye 'Igbakeji Òrìṣà' (deputy/representative of the deities) fi hàn pé Oba ni a bọ̀wọ̀ fún gẹ́gẹ́ bí ẹni tí ó dúró fún àwọn Òrìṣà àti baba ńlá lórí ilẹ̀ ayé, tí ipò rẹ̀ sì ní ìjìnlẹ̀ ẹ̀sìn àti ìṣèlú méjèèjì
questions.explanation: Traditional Yoruba kingship carries the sacred title 'Igbakeji Òrìṣà' — deputy of the deities — reflecting that the Oba's authority is both political and spiritual, positioning him as a sacred link between the ancestors/divinities and the living community.

questions.subject: Yoruba
questions.text: Kini Ogbóni (Reformed Ogboni Fraternity/Osugbo) ninu eto iselu ibile Yoruba, ati ipa wo ni won ko ninu ijọba ilu?
options: Ogbóni jẹ́ ẹgbẹ́ àwọn ọmọdé tí kò ní ipa kankan nínú ìjọba ìlú
Ogbóni jẹ́ orúkọ mìíràn fún egúngún
Ogbóni jẹ́ ẹgbẹ́ tí a dá sílẹ̀ láti kọ orin Ìjálá nìkan
Ogbóni jẹ́ ẹgbẹ́ àṣírí àwọn àgbà tí ó ní ipa ìdájọ́ àti ìmọ̀ràn nínú ìjọba ìlú, tí ó sì máa ń dá ìwọ̀n bí Oba kan ṣe ń lo agbára rẹ̀
questions.explanation: The Ogbóni (Òsùgbò) society was a council of elders holding judicial, ritual, and advisory authority in traditional Yoruba governance, serving as a check on the powers of the Oba and helping settle disputes and weighty communal matters.
